title: Torsion abelian sheaf on the small etale site
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme and $F$ an abelian sheaf on the small etale site of $T$, i.e. an object of $\Ab(T_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. For an integer $n\ge1$ let $F[n]=\ker(n:F\to F)$ [def-pur-abelian-sheaf-kernel] be the kernel of multiplication by $n$, the subsheaf of sections killed by $n$. Order the positive integers by divisibility; this poset is directed ($\operatorname{lcm}(n,m)$ bounds $n$ and $m$), hence a filtered small category, and for $n\mid m$ one has $F[n]\subseteq F[m]$ (since $m=(m/n)\cdot n$ as endomorphisms of $F$, the subobject $\ker n$ is contained in $\ker m$; sectionwise, $ns=0$ implies $ms=0$), so $n\mapsto F[n]$ with the inclusions is a filtered diagram in $\Ab(T_{\Et})$; it has a colimit because $\Ab(T_{\Et})$ has all small colimits [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and the inclusions $F[n]\hookrightarrow F$, which are compatible with the transition inclusions, induce a canonical map

$$
 c_F:\varinjlim_{n}F[n]\longrightarrow F
$$

from its colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] in $\Ab(T_{\Et})$. The sheaf $F$ is *torsion* (a *torsion abelian sheaf*) if $c_F$ is an isomorphism. Equivalent forms of this condition (every local section is locally killed by a positive integer; every stalk at a geometric point is a torsion abelian group), and the fact that it does not make every group $F(U)$ torsion, are stated in [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-sheaf-characterizations]; that lemma is about this definition and is a pointer, not a dependency.

split_report.summary: Checked against the unit sk-def-pbc (statement: torsion iff colim_n F[n] -> F is an isomorphism; equivalently torsion geometric stalks / locally killed local sections; weaker than F(U) torsion) and Stacks etale-cohomology Section 0DDB and Lemma 03SA (2), where torsion sheaves are used as F = union of the F[n] (Stacks gives no formal definition). Every notion is named by a node: Ab(T_et) [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves, Mathlib leaf], F[n] = ker(n) [def-pur-abelian-sheaf-kernel, Mathlib leaf], colimit and canonical map [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit, Mathlib leaf]; integers ordered by divisibility need no node. Claims inside the definition: the divisibility poset is directed (lcm, elementary); F[n] subset F[m] for n | m (m = (m/n) n, elementary, now written out); existence of the colimit is the clause 'it has all small colimits' of def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves (Mathlib instance HasColimitsOfSize (Sheaf J D), Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Limits.lean:228, read), now cited in the text; compatibility of the inclusions with the transition maps (elementary). The equivalent characterizations are in the existing statement node lem-weil-pbc-torsion-sheaf-characterizations (created earlier today by the worker of def-weil-pbc-property), cited by name in the statement and recorded in pointers, not stmt_deps, because it has this node in its stmt_deps. Four more Mathlib searches (leansearch, loogle, leanfinder, grep): no torsion sheaf in Mathlib; the node stays a definition with no Mathlib match. Lean of slopmaster2: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsTorsionSheaf (WeilConjectures/SixFunctors/Etale/BaseChangeTheorems/TorsionSheaf.lean:83-86) is the geometric-stalk form, for sheaves of Lambda-modules, at points Spec Omega -> X with Omega separably closed; it is equivalent to this node for Lambda = Z only through the characterization lemma, so it is not attached.
